capitals.name: Mauritsstad (Recife)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Mauritsstad, 'today part of Recife'; the town was captured by 3 March 1630, and Olinda by 16 February.

correction.text: Olinda and Recife: 'the GWC gained control of Olinda by 16 February 1630' and 'Recife and António Vaz followed by March 3'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the colony of New Holland begins 16 February 1630 ('Established' in the infobox). Cliopatria's first Brazilian cells are in 1632 inside its New Netherland row.

correction.text: the 23 Pernambuco and Paraíba cells of Cliopatria's 1632 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe from the New Netherland row's wrong 1632 shape (see that dossier). Portuguese resistance under Matias de Albuquerque 'slowed Dutch fort-building' in 1630-1637; the page gives no extent for these years.

correction.text: the coast 'from Rio Grande do Norte to Cabo de Santo Agostinho' ('By 1634 the Dutch controlled the coast') plus the 1635 strongholds: Cliopatria's 1636 shape (Pernambuco 26, Paraíba 53, Rio Grande do Norte 69, Alagoas 2 cells)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria jumps from 23 to 150 cells in 1636, the page dates the coastal control to 1634 and Porto Calvo to 1635, so the 1636 shape is used two years early (researcher's reading). Area of the shape about 38,000 km2.

correction.text: the 1634 shape plus the captaincy of Ceará, which Maurice of Nassau 'captured' within 1637 (Cliopatria's Ceará cells appear only in its 1642 shape)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Maurice arrived on 23 January 1637 and governed until 'recalled ... in 1644'. The page does not give the extent actually held in Ceará (a fort); the whole Cliopatria Ceará piece is used.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1642 shape, the widest extent: 'In 1641, the Dutch captured the captaincy of Maranhão, extending control to the coast between the Amazon and São Francisco rivers' (Dutch–Portuguese War page: 'between Maranhão and Sergipe')

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the shape (Ceará 317, Maranhão 221, Rio Grande do Norte 170, Paraíba 160, Piauí 65, Pernambuco 32 cells; 967 cells, about 244,000 km2 in Brazil) is a year late: 1641 in the page, 1642 in Cliopatria. It has no Sergipe, which the war page names as the southern limit. The page: the Dutch conquered 'almost half of Brazil's settled European area at the time'.

correction.text: the 1634 coastal shape again after the northern captaincies fall away: 'the GWC faced a major uprising of Portuguese planters in June 1645'; the page says the revolt was 'virtually confining the Dutch to the fortified urban perimeters of coastal cities'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Still in that year, the Dutch abandoned São Luís' (war page). The Ceará and Piauí cells also go in Cliopatria's 1645 shape; neither page dates that loss. The 150-cell shape is wider than the page's 'fortified urban perimeters' (soft).

correction.text: Recife and its perimeter (9 Pernambuco cells), to the capitulation of 26 January 1654, after Itamaracá was abandoned on 13 December 1647 and the Dutch were routed at Guararapes in April 1648 and February 1649

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's 9-cell shape runs to 1658, four years past the capitulation; the Treaty of The Hague (6 August 1661) merely 'formally ceded' New Holland.

ledger.note: 1630 (16 February): the Dutch take Olinda. 'the GWC gained control of Olinda by 16 February 1630'; 'Recife and António Vaz followed by March 3'. The infobox: 'Established: 16 February 1630'. The Dutch had held Bahia only in 1624-25.

region.text: the coast from Rio Grande do Norte to Cabo de Santo Agostinho

ledger.note: 1634: the coast is Dutch. 'By 1634 the Dutch controlled the coast from Rio Grande do Norte to Cabo de Santo Agostinho.'

region.text: Porto Calvo and two other strongholds

ledger.note: 1635: strongholds in the south. 'In 1635 they took Porto Calvo and two other strongholds.' The page does not name the captaincy; Alagoas is the researcher's reading. [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed from the whole of Alagoas (94 cells) to its 2 cells in the Cliopatria 1636 shape that keyframes 2-3 draw (Porto Calvo).]
1637: Maurice of Nassau, who arrived on 23 January, takes Ceará: 'Within the year, Maurice of Nassau captured the captaincy of Ceará'; Elmina on the Gold Coast was also targeted that year.

region.text: the captaincy of Maranhão, 'extending control to the coast between the Amazon and São Francisco rivers'

ledger.note: 1641: the Dutch take Maranhão. 'In 1641, the Dutch captured the captaincy of Maranhão'; 'by 1641, the Dutch captured São Luís' (war page), leaving them 'controlling northwestern Brazil'. Piauí is the researcher's reading of the coast to the São Francisco. [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed from the whole of Maranhão and Piauí (1,913 cells) to their 286 cells in the Cliopatria 1642 shape that keyframe 4 draws (the coast the page names).]

1645: the north is given up. 'Still in that year, the Dutch abandoned São Luís.' [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed to the 221 Maranhão cells of the Cliopatria 1642 shape, the land gained in 1641.]

region.text: Ceará and Piauí, which Cliopatria's 1645 shape drops

ledger.note: 1645: Cliopatria drops the Ceará and Piauí cells. Neither page dates the loss of Ceará; the year is Cliopatria's (page silent). [Reviewer am-06-c, 2026-10-19: region narrowed from the whole of Ceará and Piauí (1,334 cells) to their 382 cells in the Cliopatria 1642 shape.]

ledger.note: 1645 (June): the planters rise. 'the GWC faced a major uprising of Portuguese planters in June 1645'; 'In 1645, most of Dutch Brazil revolted under the leadership of João Fernandes Vieira' (war page).

region.text: Itamaracá island, which 'the Dutch had already abandoned ... on 13 December 1647'
Paraíba and Rio Grande do Norte, the Dutch reduced to Recife

ledger.note: 1648: Cliopatria's shape shrinks to nine Pernambuco cells. 'In April 1648, the Portuguese routed the expeditionary force at the First Battle of Guararapes'; 'In February 1649, the Portuguese again routed the Dutch at the Second Battle of Guararapes'. The pages do not date the loss of the northern coast, so the year is Cliopatria's.

region.text: Recife and the last Dutch holdings

ledger.note: 1654 (26 January): New Holland ends. 'On 26 January 1654, the Dutch surrendered and signed the capitulation' (the infobox says 28 January); 'their final expulsion from Recife in 1654' (war page).
1654 (January): the nine-year war ends with the capitulation. The Treaty of The Hague of 6 August 1661 'formally ceded' New Holland and Portugal agreed to pay eight million guilders.
1654: Dutch Brazil ends after twenty-four years; its lands pass to Portugal. Cliopatria keeps nine Pernambuco cells to 1658 (in its New Netherland row).

wars.name: Dutch–Portuguese War (Brazilian theatre)

zones.text: north-east Brazil from Maranhão to Sergipe

wars.outcome: Portuguese victory: the 1645 planters' uprising, Guararapes (April 1648, February 1649), the capitulation of 26 January 1654 and the Treaty of The Hague (6 August 1661), by which Portugal agreed to pay eight million guilders.
wars.note: The page dates the whole war 1598 to 1663; the Brazilian theatre is 1630-1654. Luanda, Benguela and the Gold Coast belong to other Dutch possessions.

certainty.note: Coastal captaincies, forts and plantation zones; the pages give no frontier and the page says that after 1645 the Dutch were confined 'to the fortified urban perimeters of coastal cities'.

sources.title: Dutch–Portuguese War
sources.note: São Luís taken 1641 and abandoned 1645; the revolt of 1645; final expulsion 1654; the war 1598-1663; limit at Sergipe.

notes: Not a Cliopatria row. Dutch Brazil is drawn by Cliopatria inside its New Netherland row (1632..1658, cells in Pernambuco, Paraíba, Rio Grande do Norte, Ceará, Maranhão and Piauí); the new-netherland dossier removes it and this dossier carries it with the same cells. The portuguese-empire dossier (am-06-a) lists 'dutch-brazil [1630, 1654]' under counterparts needing a dossier and uses dutch-republic as its counterpart; its events for 1641, 1645 and 1654 match this one. Written by am-06-c as a direct counterpart of the New Netherland row; am-06-x may also carry it (the later file wins). Unsettled: the Cliopatria shape is a year late in 1642 and 1648, early in 1636; the lost Ceará and Piauí have no page; the infobox gives 28 January 1654 and the text 26 January. Sergipe, Luanda and Natal are not on the pages. Wikidata id left null. Page budget: two pages.
